stories.title: After 'unprecedented honeymoon', UK PM faces lawmakers for first time
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham will face lawmakers in the House of Commons on September 1 for the first time since becoming UK leader six weeks ago. This comes as the wars in Europe and the Middle East weighing on his promise to kick-start the economy and ease the cost of living. Andy Burnham has enjoyed quite a long time without facing lawmakers due to the summer recess. FRANCE 24's Benedicte Paviot tells us more.

stories.title: Iran to respond militarily if US tightens blockade — parliament speaker
stories.summary: Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf believes the United States is currently focusing more on the psychological aspect of its economic war against Iran
article_sentences: Iran considers the US naval blockade an act of military aggression and will respond in kind, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, speaker of the Islamic Republic’s unicameral parliament, the Majlis, said.
"If they tighten the blockade, we will certainly respond militarily, and everyone will lose.
If the enemy decides to prevent us from exporting oil from the Persian Gulf, no one will be able to export oil," Ghalibaf said in a video address to Iranians.

In his view, the United States is currently focusing more on the psychological aspect of its economic war against Iran, as a significant portion of the newly announced sanctions had already been imposed before.
Earlier, US President Donald Trump announced the start of an "economic warfare and isolation" against Iran on an unprecedented scale.
He also warned that countries whose financial institutions, businesses, airports or state entities support Tehran would face serious economic consequences from the United States.

stories.title: From North Korea to ICE: Photojournalist David Guttenfelder on the front lines in Minneapolis
stories.summary: David Guttenfelder from The New York Times has spent 35 years photographing history around the world. Now, he is documenting it at home. The award-winning photojournalist is known for his work in Rwanda, North Korea and conflict zones across the globe. This year, he turned his camera on Minneapolis, documenting the federal immigration crackdown and deadly clashes involving ICE. His exhibition "The People of Minneapolis vs. ICE" is currently on show at the Visa pour l'Image photojournalism festival in Perpignan.

stories.title: Uniform orbit inclination for Russian, Indian, US stations to make flights safe — expert
stories.summary: Sergey Yazev noted that since 1967, Soviet and later Russian manned spacecraft have used orbits with an inclination of 51.6 degrees relative to Earth's equatorial reference plane
article_sentences: A uniform orbital inclination for the orbits in which Russian, Indian, and US space stations are planned to be deployed could enhance crew safety by enabling flights and exchanges between the stations, Sergey Yazev, a leading researcher at the Institute of Solar-Terrestrial Physics of the Siberian Branch of the Russian Academy of Sciences and a professor at Irkutsk State University, told TASS.
He noted that since 1967, Soviet and later Russian manned spacecraft have used orbits with an inclination of 51.6 degrees relative to Earth's equatorial reference plane.
The International Space Station (ISS), which is currently operating at the same inclination and is scheduled to be deorbited and crash into the Pacific Ocean in 2030, also travels in that orbit.
"This orbit will continue to be used.

By the mid-2030s, at least three national orbital stations are planned to operate in the ‘Russian’ orbit with an inclination of 51.6 degrees: the Russian Orbital Station (ROS), the US commercial Axiom Station, and the Indian space station Bharatiya Antariksh.

A uniform orbital inclination will allow, if necessary, for flights and crew exchanges, which will increase the safety of crews in space and expand the potential capabilities of the new space infrastructure," the scientist said in a conversation with TASS.
It became known last week that India has approved the first module of the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (BAS), a proposed Indian space station planned for completion by 2035.
The station is designed as a low-Earth orbit platform and is linked to India’s human spaceflight program under the Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO).
